notes: The inventory pages were not included in the PDF provided, so no Element IDs could be read. Element IDs and colours were guessed from the catalogue (tan and dark red parts) by matching shapes in the pictures.

Where the catalogue had no part in the right colour, I used a catalogue type and set the colour in props. Examples: the dark red body base plate uses lego-4121741, the tan hinge plates use lego-4521427, and the tan horn cones use lego-4529236.

To avoid reusing single-use ports, I chose multi-stud types where several pieces share one part. These are the base plate b1 (2x6), the body top plate b5, the plate b6 and the horn base b14. Each piece joins at a different named stud, and the second leg attaches to b1:anti-stud.2. The stud positions are approximate.

The neck is a long dark-red piece with hinge ends. I modelled it as lego-4296142 (plate with clip end, two hinge ports) as a stand-in. Its two hinge ends join the body's front hinge plate (b7) and the head's hinge plate (b12).

Body steps 1-4 are only roughly resolved in the pictures. I assumed a 2x6 dark red base plate, tan and dark red bricks and plates stacked on it, and a 1x4 plate on top. Exact sizes and positions are approximate.

The two legs are built from the same sub-assembly (steps 5 and 6) and attach under the body base plate. The small differences in the leg stacks were not resolved. They are modelled as two identical copies.

Step 7 adds a dark red 1x4 plate (b8) with a tan hinge plate (b9). I placed it on top of the body plate b6 and treated it as the tail and back. The picture is ambiguous about which side the hinge points to.
The step 8 head is a tan 2x2 plate with a hinge plate, a 1x1 tan plate, a dark red 1x2 plate and two tan cones. The slope shaping of the head in the pictures is not modelled as a separate piece.
Page 2 shows other 4884 alternate models in the promo area. Those are not part of this build and are ignored.
